items.answer_en: Yes, in Johnson County. The county's official 2026 I Voted stickers, picked in its design contest, go to voters during early voting and on Election Day.
items.quote: The winning designs will become the official stickers distributed during early voting and on Election Day in 2026 and 2027.
items.host_label: the Johnson County Auditor & Elections Office
items.notes: Contest announcement; submissions through July 1, 2026, public vote July 8 to 31, 2026.

items.answer_en: In Johnson County, if you vote early during the Voting After Dark evening hours for the November 3 election, you can get a special I Voted After Dark sticker after 5 p.m.
items.quote: Special “I Voted After Dark” stickers will be available only after 5:00 PM.
items.notes: Published Oct 5, 2026, for the Nov 3, 2026 general election. Evening sites: Auditor's Office Oct 26 to 28, Iowa City Public Library and others (see saved page).

items.answer_en: In Sedgwick County, the 2026 student-designed I Voted sticker comes with your advance by mail ballot, so look for it in the envelope.
items.quote: “Thousands of Sedgwick County residents who participate in the 2026 elections will have the opportunity to wear stickers they get at the polls or in an advance by mail ballot,” Rainwater said.
items.notes: April 1, 2026 release (page now labeled Archived). Quote is the Election Commissioner's statement; covers the 2026 elections, so the November general is included.

items.answer_en: Check your mail ballot packet. The DC Board of Elections lists an instruction sheet with an I Voted sticker as one of the four items you should receive.
items.quote: An Instruction Sheet with “I Voted” Sticker (4)
items.notes: Live page read Oct 24, 2026 (current instructions, not tied to one election). The quote is a list item under 'Check that you have all the contents of your Mail Ballot Packet. You should have received the following items:'. DC is one jurisdiction, so the District-wide statement is not a county-as-state problem. Replaces the June 2026 primary PDF from batch 1.

items.answer_en: In Cochise County, early ballot packets for the July 2026 primary included a county sticker. The county has not said on its site whether the November packets do too.
items.quote: A very small group of voters received a Yuma County "I Voted Early" sticker instead of the appropriate Cochise County sticker in the ballot packet they received.
items.host_label: the Cochise County Recorder's Office and Elections Department
items.notes: Posted June 30, 2026 (primary). Re-read with curl this run (200), quote confirmed verbatim. Also shows Yuma County packets carry an 'I Voted Early' sticker, but no Yuma page found. Pima's 2026 General Election insert PDF (recorder.pima.gov/docs/2026/260721_2026 General Election Insert_Web.pdf) returned 403 to curl and WebFetch, not in Wayback: blocked.

items.answer_en: In Somerville, the city's Elections Division posts its I Voted sticker as an image you can download and print at home or share online.
items.quote: Early and mail-in voters can have stickers too - here's how.
items.host_label: the City of Somerville Elections Division
items.notes: Page has no date; it says 'this year' and is live on Oct 24, 2026. Fuller sentence: 'we've shared a downloadable image you can use to print your own sticker at home or share online to tell everyone you've participated in the election process this year.'

items.answer_en: If you vote by mail in Montana, the Secretary of State's office has an I Voted sticker image you can save and post online.
items.quote: Save the image below and post it on your website, social media, or wherever you’d like! Let everyone know that you voted.
items.notes: Live page returned 403 to curl; read from Wayback snapshot of April 12, 2026. The page also says 'The image below is not the property of the Montana Secretary of State's Office.' Digital image, not a physical sticker; the page does not name mail voters.

items.answer_en: In San Luis Obispo County, the four 2026 student-designed stickers are at the San Luis Obispo and Atascadero Elections Offices, and every polling place hands them out on November 3.
items.quote: All four of the new stickers will be available at both the San Luis Obispo and Atascadero Elections Offices beginning May 4, and they will be distributed at all polling locations throughout the county on Election Day, June 2, and again on November 3.
items.host_label: the San Luis Obispo County Clerk-Recorder (SLO County Elections)
items.notes: Spring 2026 release. May 4 was the start of primary voting at the elections offices; the release does not say 'early voting' or confirm office availability during the November early period, so it supports office pickup plus Nov 3 polls, not an explicit early-voting handout.
